messages:
deploy-bot: release pipeline halted for release v2.14.0 (pipeline #8342). SBOM license mismatch + new vuln findings from vuln-scan.
anika: saw the alert, thanks. what's the exact blocker? can we get the SBOM diff?
devon: deploy-bot posted summary in the build status, but need the raw SBOM to triage.
deploy-bot: sbom-check: FAILED -> licenses: UNKNOWN in /lib/third_party/foo@1.2.3
deploy-bot: vuln-scan: HIGH -> CVE-2026-12345 present in foo@1.2.3 (possible remote exec)
jamie: ugh. foo is a transitive dep brought in by our telemetry lib. transitive bump landed in rc branch.
anika: is the CVE exploitable in our runtime? any evidence of active exploit?
security-team: quick read: CVE-2026-12345 affects versions <1.3.0 when used with feature-x enabled. We don't enable feature-x by default but need runtime config check.
sre-oncall: can we run an env-limited canary to validate? or does policy mandate pin/rollback?
devon: deploybot's policy flagged it because license was UNKNOWN + critical CVE. The policy here requires either pin to digest with proven SBOM provenance or explicit exemption signed by security.
jamie: we can pin the base image digest for the canary and isolate egress, but the SBOM entry still shows UNKNOWN license for that artifact. I can try to regenerate SBOM with --include-transitives.
anika: please regenerate and attach diff. if it's a false positive license scanner, security can approve an exception but they need artifact provenance (build id + signature) and a mitigation plan.
security-team: ok. evidence needed: (1) SBOM diff showing artifact provenance and resolved license classification OR vendor clarification, (2) risk assessment for CVE (exploitability + attack surface), (3) mitigation: canary config + automatic rollback trigger.
jamie: regenerating SBOM now. running: `./tools/generate-sbom --build-id=8342 --include-transitives --format=spdx` -> will paste output.
deploy-bot: note: change window for this release is next Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. current policy allows emergency canary within same day only with security approval.
devon: if security approves emergency canary, we should restrict to one region and route <5% traffic, and enable debug tracing and token pruning.
security-team: agreed. propose: EU region only, 3-hour canary, 1% traffic, strict egress NAT, and watch keys. If any error or increase in error rate >0.5pp rollback automatically.
jamie: SBOM regen done, snippet:
```
Package: foo@1.2.3
License: MIT
Provenance: build-8342 digest:sha256:abcd1234ef... signer:ci-builder
Transitive via: telemetry@4.5.6
```
jamie: license now shows MIT (scanner false-positive earlier). attaching full sbom link: https://artifacts/internal/sbom/8342.spdx
anika: good. security, can you confirm scanner false-positive and sign off on temporary canary with mitigations above?
security-team: we validated provenance and the license correction. For CVE: exploit requires feature-x + admin port open; our default build disables feature-x and admin port is behind firewall. Residual risk low but not zero.
security-team: approval: CONDITIONAL. Allow emergency canary with constraints: EU-only, 1% traffic, 3 hour max, auto-rollback on error signals. Must create an incident ticket and add post-mortem action to upgrade foo to >=1.3.0 within 7 days.
devon: I'll create a change ticket and the canary runbook now. also will pin the runtime image to digest `sha256:abcd1234ef...`.
sre-oncall: I'll wire the rollback trigger to the deploy job metrics and ensure runbook is front-and-center for oncall.
anika: product: aware of potential delay in release notes? Should we add a short note about temporary canary and follow-up upgrade?
jamie: yes, I'll add a note and follow-up item to the release notes draft: "Temporarily limited canary due to third-party CVE; full rollout postponed pending upgrade." Keep it high level.
devon: timeline: SBOM diff + security signoff done -> canary scheduled in 30 minutes into EU. change ticket: CHG-2026-8342. will post link when ready.
deploy-bot: action items: CHG-2026-8342 created by devon, canary schedule set to 2200123500, pinned image digest applied, auto-rollback hook enabled.
security-team: ack. monitoring hooks: cpu/latency/error-rate/auth-failures/unknown-headers. oncall pager if any > threshold.
jamie: will open PR to upgrade foo to 1.3.1 and target next patch release; tagging SRE and Security for review.
anika: thanks everyone. unless anything else, proceed with controlled canary and we'll reconvene in 2 hours for go/no-go.
security-team: noted. logging the exception and conditions in compliance tracker.
sre-oncall: starting canary now -> https://monitoring/graph?job=canary-8342
anika: thumbs up. good job turning this around quickly :thumbsup:
